newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Harvest says JSE blocked Coronation offer.
newsitem.headline: Harvest says JSE blocked Coronation offer.

text.p: South Africa's Harvest Securities Ltd said on Monday it was removing a cautionary announcement from its shares after an offer from Coronation Holdings Ltd was blocked.
The firm said the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) could not approve the offer by Coronation as it did not confirm with its rules to protect the pre-emptive rights of shareholders.
"In consequence Coronation withdrew and made other arrangements," the firm said.

The deal had consisted of the issue to Harvest of one billion rands worth of Coronation "N" shares, the issue by Harvest to Coronation of 112 million new shares and an offer by Coronation to buy all Harvest shares for 890 cents each.
On June 26 Coronation Holdings Ltd said it had agreed to create a new black empowerment investment company, African Harvest Ltd, with National Empowerment Corp.
African Harvest, which will have a capital base of one billion rand, will be jointly controlled by NE Corp and Coronation via a holding company, African Harvest Holdings (Pty) Ltd.
It also plans to raise some 1.25 billion rand before expenses by way of a renounceable rights offer of new "N" (non-voting) shares.
